questions.def: "Called off" means cancelled or postponed.
questions.question: The meeting was called ___ due to unforeseen circumstances.

questions.def: "Knock down" means to demolish.
questions.question: They decided to ___ the old house before building a new one.

questions.def: "Put out" means to extinguish a fire.
questions.question: We need to ___ the fire before leaving.

questions.def: "Came into" means to inherit.
questions.question: He came ___ a lot of money when his uncle died.

questions.def: "Break into" means to enter forcefully or successfully.
questions.question: The company is trying to ___ new markets.

questions.def: "Turned down" means to refuse an offer.
questions.question: He ___ the job offer because of the low salary.

questions.def: "Takes after" means to resemble someone.

questions.def: "Broke down" means stopped functioning.

questions.def: "Get through" means to complete or finish something.

questions.def: "Looking into" means to investigate.

questions.def: "Back out" means to withdraw from a commitment.
questions.question: Don't ___ on your promises.

questions.def: "Call off" means to cancel.

questions.def: "Put on" means to gain weight.

questions.def: "Brush up on" means to revise or improve a skill.
questions.question: I need to ___ my French before my trip.

questions.def: "Looked up" means contacted.
questions.question: I ___ my old school friend yesterday.

questions.def: "Ended up" means to eventually do or be.

questions.def: "Turn down" means to decrease the volume.
questions.question: Can you ___ the music a little?

questions.def: "Worked out" means to have a successful result.

questions.def: "Ran into" means to encounter.

questions.def: "Butting in" means interrupting or interfering.

questions.def: "Took on" means to accept a responsibility.

questions.def: "Fell through" means failed to happen.

questions.def: "Called off" means cancelled. Other options are incorrect phrasal verbs.
questions.question: The meeting was ___ due to the speaker's illness.

questions.def: "Give up" means to stop doing something. Other phrasal verbs are incorrect.
questions.question: I'm trying to ___ smoking, but it's difficult.

questions.def: "Have looked" implies an action completed over a period of time.
questions.question: I ___ my keys everywhere, but I can't find them.

questions.def: "Take on" means to accept a challenge or responsibility.
questions.question: He decided to ___ the challenge despite the risks.

questions.def: "Take on" in this context means to hire or employ.
questions.question: The company is planning to ___ new staff next year.

questions.def: "Come out" means to become known or revealed.
questions.question: The truth will ___ eventually.

questions.def: "Cut someone off" means to interrupt them.
questions.question: Don't ___ me ___, but I think you're wrong.
